name: DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: DigitalOcean provides on-demand cloud infrastructure (compute, storage, networking) and managed application, container and database services to developers, startups and small and mid-sized businesses worldwide [4]. Under CEO Paddy Srinivasan the company now brands itself the 'AI-Native Cloud' built for inference and agentic workloads; AI customer ARR grew 212% YoY to $234M in Q2 2026, and its Inference Engine, launched in April 2026, has more than 6,000 customers [2]. Q2 2026 revenue was ~$281M (+29% YoY), and management guides FY2026 revenue to ~$1.17-1.18B with growth of at least 35% exiting Q4 [1]. Q3 2026 results had not yet been reported at the screen date.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): DigitalOcean has repositioned from a simple developer VPS cloud into an 'AI-Native Cloud' for inference and agentic workloads, opening a new revenue stream that reached $234M of AI customer ARR (+212% YoY) by Q2 2026 [2]. That is one significant pivot, but the core cloud remains the majority of revenue. AI Deployment (2/2): AI products are shipping at scale: the Inference Engine (launched April 2026) has 6,000+ customers, inference services grew nearly 800% YoY, and inference plus core cloud products make up more than 70% of AI customer ARR [2]. Market Share (1/2): DigitalOcean is a meaningful, focused player in developer and SMB cloud, but it is far smaller than the hyperscalers and competes with GPU neoclouds; no share-leadership data was found. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management guides to at least 35% growth exiting Q4 2026 and added a CRO and CMO in June 2026 for 'the next chapter', but no specific next-generation product launches with dates were identified [1][2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FY2025 R&D of $161.6M was 17.9% of revenue, roughly in line with infrastructure-software peers [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): DigitalOcean's purpose has long centered on simplifying the cloud for developers and small businesses, and its current positioning as an AI-native cloud for builders identifies what it does and for whom, but the language has shifted with the AI pivot and does not yet articulate a distinctive purpose beyond that [2]. Community Impact (1/2): The company is presenting partner of Hacktoberfest, which in 2026 became 300+ community-hosted 'Fests' focused on open models and open-source agents [3]. Credit is partial: no dollar-quantified giving was found, and the 2020 Hacktoberfest drew widespread maintainer criticism for incentivizing spam pull requests [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP data shows zero open-market purchases since 2023 and heavy selling: 24 insider sales disposing of ~3.85M shares in Q2 2026 and 7 more sales in Q3 2026 [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth metrics. ROE of 62.3% (2x weight) scores 1.0, though it is inflated by a FY2025 income-tax benefit of $52.6M and a small equity base (book value ~$8.90/share) [4][5]. Revenue growth of 28.6% YoY scores 1.0, and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 23.1% (FY2020 $318M to FY2025 $901M, derived from FMP annual statements) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [5]. Profit margin of 23.3% scores 1.0. D/E of 212.5% scores 0.38, and the forward P/E of 49.1x scores 0.27 [4]. Forward PEG is excluded (null): the provider's forward PEG is -1.24 because consensus EPS falls after the one-time tax benefit (yfinance earnings growth -24.5%), so it is not meaningful. Weighted sum 6.65 / 8 = 8.3, rounded to 8. Liquidity floor cleared at ~$242M average daily dollar volume. Note: TTM free cash flow is thin (P/FCF ~710x) because capex consumes nearly all operating cash flow [5].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): DigitalOcean sells compute, GPU and inference capacity, so it is AI infrastructure rather than a target of AI substitution. AI-native demand is the main source of its acceleration, with inference services up nearly 800% YoY [2]. Management argues that cheaper open-source models (cost per token 'about 90% cheaper') expand its market rather than threaten it [2]. The residual risk is competitive: hyperscalers and GPU neoclouds compete for the same inference workloads, and pricing pressure on commodity GPU capacity could compress margins. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI customer ARR was $234M in Q2 2026, up 212% YoY [2].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would see a company with a real founding cause (making the cloud simple for developers and small businesses) that is now testing whether that cause can carry it through the AI era. The pivot to an 'AI-Native Cloud' is consistent with serving builders, and management is spending heavily on capacity (capex consumes nearly all operating cash flow) to stay relevant [2][5]. Steady insider selling and the commercial framing of the June 2026 executive hires ('commercial firepower') suggest a company that is still partly playing for the next quarter [2][6].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Since its founding in 2012, DigitalOcean has built its identity around simplicity for individual developers and small teams. Its long-running tutorial library, community programs and Hacktoberfest reflect a service orientation beyond selling compute [3]. The cause has not yet been tested across decades, and the 2026 rebranding around 'inference and agentic workloads' risks making it about a technology cycle rather than the people it serves [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): No Glassdoor data or culture red flags surfaced in research. The June 2026 additions of a Chief Revenue Officer, Chief Marketing Officer and a third executive add commercial depth without signs of disruptive turnover [2]. With no evidence of exceptional empowerment or tenure, this scores as adequate.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management's competitive messaging differentiates against bare-metal GPU providers by stressing that 70-85% of AI ARR comes from inference and core cloud rather than bare metal [2]. That is positioning against rivals; no commentary was found about learning from what hyperscalers or neoclouds do better.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Moving from general-purpose droplets to an inference-first, AI-native platform is a meaningful strategic shift that redirected capex and the product roadmap, and inference is now the majority of AI ARR [2]. The company still sells cloud infrastructure to the same developer and SMB base, so this is an adjacent evolution rather than abandoning a core business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership has accepted near-zero TTM free cash flow (FCF/OCF ~4%) to build GPU and inference capacity ahead of demand, a costly bet on long-term relevance [5]. Offsetting that, the balance sheet carries D/E of 212%, so the capacity bet is partly debt-funded rather than paid for out of earnings, which limits room to keep investing through a downturn [4].

investment_thesis: DigitalOcean is now an AI infrastructure growth story with real profitability. Q2 2026 revenue rose ~29% YoY to ~$281M with adjusted EPS of $0.45 against a $0.26 consensus, and Q3 guidance of $304-307M was above the $294M consensus [1]. FY2026 revenue is guided to ~$1.17-1.18B (+30-31%), with growth of at least 35% exiting Q4 [1]. AI customer ARR of $234M (+212%) is mostly inference rather than commoditized bare-metal GPU rental, and the 6,000+ Inference Engine customers extend DigitalOcean's strength with developers into agentic AI [2]. The stock has fallen to $89.79 from a 52-week high of $187.50, so much of the earlier froth is gone, and the Inspire score of 42 (ALIGNED, no negatives) supports faith-aligned ownership [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation, leverage and cash conversion. At 49x forward earnings and ~10x sales, the stock prices in sustained 30%+ growth [4][5]. Capex now absorbs nearly all operating cash flow (TTM P/FCF ~710x), and D/E of 212% leaves little cushion if GPU utilization or pricing weakens [5]. Consensus EPS is expected to decline (yfinance earnings growth -24.5%) as the FY2025 tax benefit laps, and insiders sold ~3.85M shares in Q2 2026 alone [4][6]. The stock fell ~6.5% even after the Q2 beat-and-raise, showing how sensitive it is to any deceleration [1].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results versus $304-307M revenue guidance, and confirmation of the 35%+ exit-rate growth target for Q4 2026 [1]
Inference Engine scaling — 6,000+ customers within months of its April 2026 launch, with inference services growing ~800% YoY, driving higher-margin AI ARR [2]
New commercial leadership (CRO, CMO hired June 2026) moving up-market to larger AI-native customers and raising net revenue retention [2]
key_risks: GPU capex intensity — near-zero TTM free cash flow means a slowdown in AI demand or GPU price deflation would quickly pressure returns on billions in deployed capacity [5]
Leverage — D/E of 212% raises refinancing risk if the equity multiple keeps compressing from the $187.50 52-week high [4]
Competitive squeeze — hyperscalers and GPU neoclouds compete aggressively on inference pricing, which could erode DigitalOcean's simplicity premium with SMB and developer customers [2]
